title: Peter Thiel slams Obama, Pope Leo in new ‘Antichrist’ lectures
source_used: New York Post and Gizmodo, both relaying Politico
key_facts: Politico obtained recordings of Peter Thiel's 'Antichrist' lecture series in Nashville, a four-part ticketed series.
The lectures were on 28 Sep and Monday 5 Oct 2026, according to the New York Post.
Thiel said Obama and Pope Leo XIV want to 'boost their own popularity' because AI is politically unpopular.
He suggested the pope's focus on AI distracts from the church's child sex abuse scandals.
The New York Post says Obama recently urged Democrats to come up with a comprehensive approach to regulating AI; the pope's first encyclical was about AI.
Thiel's lectures cast AI regulation advocates and a 'one-world government' as antichrist figures.
Thiel's representatives, and those of Obama, Vance and the Vatican, did not comment to Politico.
quote_evidence: “Many people know that AI is politically unpopular and want to leverage that to boost their own popularity,” Thiel reportedly said in Nashville.
“Both Obama and the pope fall into this category. Obama knows the Democrats have no ideas, but they can at least oppose AI.”
Thiel’s attacks on the church could complicate life for Vance, a converted Catholic, Politico pointed out.
why_it_matters_hint: A major tech investor frames AI regulation in religious terms and attacks the pope, with possible political effects.
event_date: Lectures 28 Sep and 5 Oct 2026; Politico report 8 Oct 2026
notes: Politico returned 403; read the New York Post and Gizmodo accounts, which quote Politico's recordings. Neither Politico text nor the recordings were seen directly.
